newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Democrats call for casino review.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Democrats call for casino review.

text.p: The Australian Democrats called on Thursday for a review of legal monopolies provided to casino operators, saying they may be inconsistent with competition principles in other industries.

Democrats accountability spokesman Andrew Murray said he wanted a government guarantee that there would be an investigation into legal monopolies, under which casino operators were protected, to make sure they met anti-competitive guidelines.

"If it's good enough for competition policy to be used to challenge the so-called monopoly rights of newsagents, taxi drivers and building contractors, then it must be good enough to question whether the legal casino monopolies provided to multi-millionaires should be continued to be protected," Murray said in a statement.
Major casino cities such as Las Vegas, Atlantic City and London did not have monopoly rights on gambling and there was competition between operators, he said.

"Why Australia's state governments have been allowed to set and protect statutory monopolies, while at the same time being required by federal law to pursue principles of competition policy in other areas, is an issue which needs to be closely examined."
